name: National Means-cum-Merit Scholarship Scheme (NMMSS)
organization: Department of School Education & Literacy, Ministry of Education
description: A scholarship for bright students from poor families, so they keep studying after Class 8. Selected students get money every year from Class 9 to Class 12.
eligibility: Student must study as a regular student in a Government, Government-aided or local body school. Family income must not be more than Rs 3,50,000 a year. Needs at least 55% marks in Class 7 to sit the test, and 55% in Class 8 when selected (5% less for SC/ST). Kendriya Vidyalaya, Navodaya Vidyalaya, government residential school and private school students cannot apply.
benefits: Rs 12,000 per year (Rs 1,000 per month) for up to four years, Class 9 to Class 12. Money goes straight to the student's bank account. To continue in Class 11 and 12, the student needs 60% marks in Class 10 (5% less for SC/ST) and must pass each class in the first try.
how_to_apply: 1. In Class 8, take the NMMSS selection test held by your State (usually in November). It has two papers: Mental Ability Test and Scholastic Aptitude Test. 2. Pass with at least 40% total (32% for SC/ST). 3. If selected, apply on the National Scholarship Portal and renew your application there every year.

name: PM-USP Central Sector Scheme of Scholarship for College and University Students
organization: Department of Higher Education, Ministry of Education
description: A scholarship for students from poorer families who got high marks in Class 12 and are now studying in college. It helps pay part of their daily study costs.
eligibility: Must be above the 80th percentile (top 20%) of passed students in your stream in your Class 12 board. Family income up to Rs 4.5 lakh a year. Must study a regular degree course (not distance or diploma) at a recognised college. Must not get any other scholarship or fee waiver. Students who took a gap year after Class 12 cannot apply.
benefits: Rs 12,000 per year for the first three years of graduation and Rs 20,000 per year for post-graduation. B.Tech/BE students get Rs 20,000 in the 4th year. Money is paid into your Aadhaar-linked bank account. To renew each year, you need at least 50% marks and 75% attendance.
documents: Active mobile number linked with Aadhaar
how_to_apply: 1. On the National Scholarship Portal (scholarships.gov.in), register with your mobile number and Aadhaar to get a One-Time Registration (OTR) number. 2. Log in, choose your state and 'Post-Matric', and select this scheme. 3. Upload documents and submit. 4. Make sure your college verifies it before the deadline. Applying is free.
contact: Scholarship Division, Department of Higher Education: 011-20862360, ns1-scholarship@gov.in; www.scholarships.gov.in

name: Right to Education Act - 25% free seats in private schools (Section 12(1)(c))
description: Under the Right to Education Act, private unaided schools must give at least 25% of Class 1 seats to children from weaker and disadvantaged families. These children study for free until they finish elementary school.
eligibility: Children belonging to a 'weaker section' or 'disadvantaged group' who live in the school's neighbourhood. The RTE Act gives every child aged 6 to 14 the right to free and compulsory education. Check the exact rules and income limit with your State or district education office.
benefits: Free education in a private unaided school, from Class 1 until elementary education is complete.

name: Pradhan Mantri Poshan Shakti Nirman (PM POSHAN)
organization: Department of School Education & Literacy, Ministry of Education
description: A free hot cooked meal for children in government and government-aided schools on every school day. It was earlier called the Mid-Day Meal scheme.
eligibility: Children studying in Bal Vatika (the class just before Class 1) and Classes 1 to 8 in Government and Government-aided schools. The scheme is run by State Governments, and menus differ by state.
benefits: One hot cooked meal on every school working day. Primary classes: 450 calories and 12 g protein per child per day. Upper primary classes: 700 calories and 20 g protein. States choose menus using local foods like millets and vegetables.
how_to_apply: Enrol your child in a Government or Government-aided school. The meal is given at school on all school working days.

name: Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB PM-JAY)
organization: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
description: Free hospital treatment for poor and vulnerable families, up to Rs 5 lakh per family each year, at government and listed private hospitals. Since 2024, all people aged 70 and above are also covered.
eligibility: Poor and vulnerable families identified using the Socio-Economic Caste Census 2011 (about 12 crore families), plus ASHA and Anganwadi workers and their families. No limit on family size or age. All seniors aged 70+ are eligible whatever their income, through the Ayushman Vay Vandana Card. In 2024 a few states were not in the scheme; check locally.
benefits: Up to Rs 5 lakh per family per year for hospital care, cashless at empanelled hospitals anywhere in India. Covers 3 days before and 15 days after the hospital stay (tests and medicines). Old illnesses are covered from day one. People aged 70+ get their own Rs 5 lakh cover, even if their family is already covered.
how_to_apply: Seniors aged 70+ can register at the nearest empanelled hospital, through the Ayushman app, or at www.beneficiary.nha.gov.in. Call 14555 to know more. At an empanelled hospital, treatment is cashless for eligible people.

name: Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana (PMMVY)
organization: Ministry of Women and Child Development
description: Cash help for pregnant women and new mothers, to make up for lost wages and help them rest and stay healthy before and after delivery.
eligibility: Women aged 18 years 7 months to 55 years at childbirth who meet any one condition: SC/ST; 40%+ disability; BPL or NFSA ration card; PM-JAY, e-Shram, PM-Kisan or MGNREGA job card holder; family income under Rs 8 lakh a year; or pregnant ASHA/Anganwadi worker. Not run in Telangana and Odisha, which have their own schemes.
benefits: First child: Rs 5,000 in two parts. Rs 3,000 after registering the pregnancy and at least two check-ups, and Rs 2,000 after birth registration and the baby's first vaccines (14 weeks). Second child, if a girl: Rs 6,000 in one payment after birth and vaccines. Paid to an Aadhaar-linked bank or post office account.
documents: Aadhaar-linked bank or post office account details
Proof of eligibility (any one, such as ration card, job card, e-Shram card or income certificate)
Date of last period (LMP) and check-up (ANC) dates
how_to_apply: Ask your nearest Anganwadi or ASHA worker to fill the online form for you, or register yourself on pmmvy.wcd.gov.in or the PMMVY mobile app. You can register up to 270 days after childbirth. Husband's Aadhaar is not needed.

name: Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme (IGNOAPS) - National Social Assistance Programme
description: A monthly pension for elderly people from poor (below poverty line) families. It is part of the National Social Assistance Programme.
eligibility: People aged 60 years or more who belong to families living below the poverty line (BPL). States add their own money, so the total pension is different in each state.
benefits: The Central Government gives Rs 200 per month for ages 60 to 79, and Rs 500 per month for age 80 and above. States add a top-up of Rs 50 to Rs 5,700 per month, so many states pay around Rs 1,100 in total. Paid mostly into a bank or post office account.
how_to_apply: Contact your Gram Panchayat (village) or Municipality (town). They help identify eligible people. The scheme is run by your State Government.

name: Viksit Bharat - Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) (VB-G RAM G) - replaced MGNREGA
description: A legal guarantee of paid work for rural families. From 1 July 2026 it replaced MGNREGA and gives up to 125 days of work a year instead of 100.
eligibility: Every rural household whose adult members are willing to do unskilled manual work. Old MGNREGA job cards with completed e-KYC stay valid until new Gramin Rozgar Guarantee Cards are given. States can pause work for up to 60 days in peak farm seasons, and each State runs its own scheme under the Act.
benefits: Up to 125 days of paid work per household each year. Wages are paid weekly, or within 15 days, into a bank or post office account, with extra pay if late. If work is not given in time, you get an unemployment allowance. Worksites must have drinking water, shade, first aid, and childcare when five or more small children are present.
documents: MGNREGA Job Card (e-KYC verified) or Gramin Rozgar Guarantee Card
how_to_apply: 1. If you have no job card, apply at your Gram Panchayat to register and get a new card. 2. Ask for work by speaking, in writing (Form-6), or online. 3. Work must be given within the set time; if not, you get unemployment allowance.

name: Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana 4.0 (PMKVY 4.0) - Skill India Programme
organization: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
description: Free short-term skill training for young people, with a skill certificate, to help them get jobs. It also certifies skills people already have (Recognition of Prior Learning).
eligibility: Indian citizens with a valid Aadhaar who meet the course's requirements. Short-term training: age 15 to 45. Recognition of Prior Learning (for people with work experience): age 18 to 59. Special focus on backward, border, tribal and aspirational districts.
benefits: Free skill training, with on-the-job training in many courses, and a skill certificate after you pass the assessment. One free re-assessment if you fail. Courses include new areas like AI, drones, solar energy and 5G.
how_to_apply: Register on Skill India Digital (www.skillindiadigital.gov.in) or its mobile app, and verify your profile with a mobile OTP. Training is given at Skill India Centres.

name: Scheme of Assistance to Persons with Disabilities for Purchase/Fitting of Aids and Appliances (ADIP Scheme)
organization: Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities (Divyangjan), Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
description: Gives free or low-cost aids and devices, like artificial limbs, wheelchairs, tricycles, hearing aids and learning kits, to people with disabilities from low-income families.
eligibility: Indian citizen of any age with a UDID card (or enrolment number) and a disability certificate showing at least 40% disability. Monthly income (own, or parents' for dependents) up to Rs 30,000. Must not have received help for the same aid in the last 3 years (1 year for children under 12).
benefits: Income up to Rs 22,500 a month: full cost of the aid. Income Rs 22,501 to Rs 30,000: half the cost. Motorised tricycle or wheelchair (80%+ disability, age 16+) up to Rs 50,000. Cochlear implant for young children up to Rs 7 lakh. Travel costs up to Rs 250 are also paid.
documents: UDID card or UDID enrolment number
Aadhaar number or Aadhaar enrolment ID
Income certificate (or BPL card, MGNREGA card, disability pension card, or certificate from MP/MLA/Councillor/Gram Pradhan)
how_to_apply: Go to an assessment camp in your district run by agencies like ALIMCO, or visit the nearest National Institute, Composite Regional Centre (CRC) or District Disability Rehabilitation Centre (DDRC). You can also request an aid online through the ADIP portal or mobile app; it should be given within 6 months.

name: One Stop Centre (Sakhi) and Women Helpline 181 - Mission Shakti
organization: Ministry of Women and Child Development
description: One Stop Centres (Sakhi Centres) help women facing violence or in trouble, with many services in one place. Women Helpline 181 is a 24-hour phone line that connects women to help.
eligibility: Any woman affected by violence or in distress, at home or in public. Her daughters of any age and sons up to 12 can stay with her in the temporary shelter. Girls under 18 are also helped with child protection authorities. Anyone can call 181 on behalf of a woman in distress.
benefits: At the One Stop Centre: medical aid, legal aid and advice, police help, counselling, and temporary shelter for up to 5 days, all under one roof. Helpline 181 works 24x7, links women to police, One Stop Centres, hospitals and legal services, and gives information about government schemes for women.
how_to_apply: Call 181 (Women Helpline) at any time, or 112 in an emergency. You can also go to the One Stop Centre in your district, which is usually in or near a government hospital.

name: National Food Security Act (NFSA) ration and Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana (PMGKAY)
organization: Department of Food and Public Distribution, Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution
description: Ration card holders get rice, wheat or coarse grains every month from fair price (ration) shops. Under PMGKAY these grains are completely free for five years from 1 January 2024.
eligibility: Families identified by the State Government as 'Priority Households' or 'Antyodaya Anna Yojana' (poorest) households. The Act covers up to 75% of rural people and 50% of urban people. Your State decides which families qualify.
benefits: Priority households: 5 kg of grains per person per month. Antyodaya families: 35 kg per family per month. Free of cost under PMGKAY. With One Nation One Ration Card, you can take your ration from any fair price shop in India. The Act also gives free meals to pregnant women and young children through Anganwadis.
how_to_apply: Ration cards are issued by your State Government, so apply to your State food department. The eldest woman (18 or older) in the family is made head of the household on the card. Then collect your grains every month at your fair price shop.
